name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong R+21 partisan lean in a southern Ohio seat
Incumbent David Taylor running with over $1M raised
Democratic challenger has raised only about $1,000
Prediction markets price the Republican near 97%
model.rationale: The district's R+21 lean, a first-term incumbent with a large fundraising edge, and a Democratic challenger who has raised barely a thousand dollars all point to a safe Republican hold, matching Polymarket's 97% pricing.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or major outside spending against Taylor would be the only realistic path to moving this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
David Taylor, a Republican incumbent, is seeking a full term in this heavily Republican southern Ohio district, where the partisan lean favors Republicans by roughly 21 points. He has raised about $1.1 million and enters the general election with a comfortable cash position after clearing his primary.

Democratic nominee Jennifer Mazzuckelli has run a minimal campaign, reporting just over $1,000 raised and a few hundred dollars on hand, with no outside spending or polling to suggest competitive conditions. Prediction markets price the Republican at about 97%, and no expert raters flag the race as contested. The seat is expected to remain safely in Republican hands.
